[...] [MS p.7] Le système tonal *SBB est caractérisé par deux tons distinctifs. Les langues occidentales (cf. infra) résultent toutes d’un système postérieur (*OCC) qui a développé un troisième ton vers le haut. L’apparition d’un quatrième niveau (infra-bas) est tardive et limitée (yulu, fer, gula koto).

new_statements.translation: [LLACAN] Language structure: notable features: retroflex vibrant affricate consonants; tone system (four registers). [Boyeldieu & Nougayrol 2008] The SBB languages have systems of two, three or four tone heights, whose correspondences follow specific formulas depending on whether nouns or verbs are considered. [...] The *SBB tone system is characterised by two distinctive tones. The western languages all derive from a later system (*OCC) which developed a third tone upwards. The appearance of a fourth level (extra-low) is late and limited (Yulu, Fer, Gula Koto).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Both quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators. (1) (and, the Internet Archive 20041122162226 of llacan.cnrs-bellevue.fr/francais/Rech/Langues/Fer.htm): "Structure de langue : traits remarquables : consonnes afriquées vibrantes rétroflexes; système tonal (quatre registres)." The page is a one-screen profile; it also gives autonym fɛ́r, region of Birao (northern CAR), ~4,000 speakers, classification SBB / Central Sudanic, and "la dénomination kara est courante mais impropre". No word on accent/stress. (2) (17 pp incl. HAL cover): extracted text of PDF pp.7-8 (= MS pp.6-7, page numbers printed at foot) reproduces exactly "Les langues SBB connaissent des systèmes à d…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Fer/Kara is a register-tone language with four contrastive tone levels (high, mid, low, extra-low); the accessible sources by its principal describer characterise its word prosody entirely in terms of lexical tone and make no statement about word stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Both statements are about the lexical tone system of the language as a whole; neither says anything about word stress, phrase accent or citation forms. No accessible source addresses stress at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog kara1482 'Kara (Central African Republic)' = Fer (autonym fɛ́r), also 'Kara de Birao', Dam Fer, Fertit; ISO kah. LLACAN's page states 'la dénomination kara est courante mais impropre'. Santandrea 1970 describes 'Kara' of Bahr el Ghazal (Sudan), which Glottolog and WALS treat as the same language; Boyeldieu's 1989 'Yulu/Kara' title uses 'Kara' for Fer. Not to be confused with Yulu-Binga (yulu1243), whose Kara/Nguru dialect of Sudan LLACAN calls 'une variante dialectale du yulu'.
